note.note:
History:
• 53-year-old male presents with painless swelling over the left elbow noted ~1 week ago while showering  
• Describes slight warmth and “fluid-filled” sensation; minimal tenderness adjacent to tip of olecranon, full range of motion preserved  
• Denies trauma, repetitive strain, prior similar episodes, fever, systemic symptoms, or other joint involvement  
• Occupation: desk-based; runs 2–3 times/week  
• No family history of inflammatory arthritis reported

Past Medical History:
• Osteoarthritis – GP diagnosis “a few years ago”  
• Allergy: peanuts (severity not specified)  
• Drug allergies: none known  
• Medications: none regularly

Physical Examination (video):
• Left olecranon bursal swelling visible; overlying skin dry, mildly warm compared with surrounding tissue  
• Mild focal tenderness just lateral to olecranon; no significant pain on palpation of olecranon tip  
• Elbow moves normally without restriction  
• No diffuse erythema, no obvious cellulitis, patient alert and comfortable

Impression:
• Left olecranon bursitis, likely non-septic inflammatory

Management Plan:
• Recommend OTC ibuprofen 400 mg PO twice daily with food; stop if heartburn occurs (dose/route/frequency documented)  
• Arrange phlebotomy: inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, uric acid (gout screen) – form to be mailed to patient  
• Follow-up review (video/telephone or face-to-face) ~6 days after blood draw to assess elbow and discuss results  
• Safety-net: seek urgent assessment if elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, or redness spreads (concern for septic arthritis)

Patient Summary:
Mr. Smith developed a painless, mildly warm swelling over his left elbow over the past week. Video exam is consistent with olecranon bursitis without features of acute infection. He will start anti-inflammatories and undergo blood testing; results will be reviewed at follow-up.

Key Takeaways:
• Start ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily with food.  
• Obtain blood tests as soon as the form arrives.  
• Contact GP urgently if swelling worsens, becomes very red, or increasingly painful.

Next Steps:
• Complete blood work (ESR/CRP, FBC, uric acid, rheumatologic screen).  
• Follow-up consultation in ~1 week to review results and re-examine elbow.  
• Consider in-person assessment sooner if clinical status deteriorates.
